AAON_2017q3:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about -7.4% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 4.2% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock underperformed the broad market by about 11.6 percentage points. The underperformance occurred even though the May earnings report showed improving order intake and backlog, because quarterly earnings were lower and warranty, promotional and stock-compensation costs were already pressuring profitability. During the quarter, AAON maintained its dividend and announced board changes, but no independent coverage identified those items as major stock catalysts. Backlog of $68.9 million and elevated costs were therefore both known before the August report.

Earnings Summary

AAON reported second-quarter revenue of $101.3 million, down about 1% year over year, and net income of $13.8 million, down 6.3%. Backlog increased further to $83.5 million, units sold rose about 5.3%, and warranty expense remained elevated.

Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Continued backlog growth
Backlog was already strong, but the further increase from $68.9 million to $83.5 million confirmed that order momentum continued.

Second-order driver — Persistently high warranty costs
Higher warranty expense was already known and continued to weigh directly on current profitability.

Third-order driver — Higher unit sales but limited revenue growth
Unit volume increased, but a less favorable mix of lower-priced products limited reported sales growth.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2018q4:
Prior Context

First-order driver — Evidence on operating execution
The main question was whether AAON was beginning to improve throughput after labor and manufacturing constraints.

Second-order driver — Persistent cost pressure
Warranty, labor and other operating costs continued to restrict profitability.

Third-order driver — High backlog
Demand remained strong, but the large order book was already known and therefore represented confirmation rather than a new theme.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2019q2:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about 35.9% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 9.4% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock outperformed the broad market by about 26.5 percentage points. Investors entered the May report expecting price increases, improved training and higher production to restore profitability. AAON reported first-quarter sales of approximately $113.8 million, up about 15%, and net income of $10.9 million, up sharply from $4.3 million. Backlog reached about $166 million, while pricing and improved productivity helped offset labor and material costs.

Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Sales and earnings recovery
The sharp improvement in net income and double-digit sales growth showed progress after the weak operating performance of 2018.

Second-order driver — Margin improvement
Pricing and productivity began to offset labor and raw-material inflation.

Third-order driver — Further backlog growth
Backlog continued to rise, supporting future revenue, although strong demand was already embedded in expectations.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2019q4:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about -8.4% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 1.8% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock underperformed the broad market by about 10.2 percentage points. During the quarter, broader market volatility added pressure, but the company-specific issue remained manufacturing capacity rather than demand.

AAON reported third-quarter sales of about $113.5 million, up only 0.5%, and diluted EPS of about $0.26. Management said sheet-metal production constrained sales, although new fabrication equipment was beginning to improve capacity. The company also opened a new research laboratory.

Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Production constraints
Sheet-metal capacity directly limited sales and prevented the order book from converting into stronger revenue.

Second-order driver — Only modest sales growth
Revenue growth of roughly 0.5% reinforced concerns about throughput rather than demand.

Third-order driver — New capacity and research investment
Additional fabrication equipment and the research laboratory supported longer-term growth but were less immediate than the production bottleneck.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.

AAON_2021q4:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about 15.3% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 5.1% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock outperformed the broad market by about 10.2 percentage points. The stock outperformed as demand and backlog remained strong, but the operating context deteriorated because material inflation, supply shortages and labor inefficiencies were compressing margins. Independent coverage during the quarter focused more on inflation and the broader market than on a separate company-specific event, leaving profitable conversion of backlog as the central issue.

AAON reported third-quarter revenue of about $138.6 million and EPS of roughly $0.29. Earnings missed expectations, while strong demand and backlog supported the outlook. Material inflation, supply shortages and production inefficiencies continued to pressure margins.

First-order driver — Demand and backlog resilience
The positive stock response may have reflected continued confidence in demand despite the earnings miss.

Second-order driver — Inflation and supply-chain pressure
Higher input costs and operating inefficiencies remained the main constraint on profitability.

Third-order driver — Reaction relative to expectations
The stock rose even though earnings were weak, suggesting that forward demand or the perceived temporary nature of cost pressure mattered more than the headline miss.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2022q3:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about 23.9% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 0.4% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock outperformed the broad market by about 23.5 percentage points. AAON substantially outperformed the market as backlog and pricing supported expectations for strong revenue growth. During the quarter, founder Norman Asbjornson retired as executive chairman, the company announced other leadership changes and maintained its dividend. Operationally, investors were still focused on whether price increases could catch up with inflation and whether BASX could be integrated efficiently.

Earnings Summary

AAON reported second-quarter revenue of about $208.8 million, up 45.1%, while EPS declined to about $0.30. BASX contributed $24.6 million of sales and legacy volume also increased. Backlog reached a record level, but material, component, labor and freight costs reduced gross margin. Debt and working-capital needs increased with expansion.

Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Record revenue and backlog
The scale of sales growth and strong BASX demand were the clearest positive developments.

Second-order driver — Earnings and margin pressure
Despite large revenue growth, higher costs caused EPS to decline, showing that pricing and productivity had not fully caught up with inflation.

Third-order driver — BASX integration and leadership transition
BASX created additional growth opportunities while the leadership changes added a smaller execution consideration.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2023q1:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about 18.7% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 5.7% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock outperformed the broad market by about 13.0 percentage points. The stock outperformed as investors anticipated that price increases and improving supply conditions would restore margins after a difficult 2022. Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Large earnings and revenue beat
Both EPS and revenue exceeded consensus by meaningful margins.

Second-order driver — Margin recovery
Pricing, reduced supply disruption and improved production efficiency reversed much of the earlier profitability pressure.

Third-order driver — Record production and backlog
Strong output and backlog increased confidence that demand could continue converting into revenue.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
AAON_2024q1:

The large improvement in gross margin demonstrated continued pricing and operating-efficiency gains.

Second-order driver — Strong but moderating growth outlook

Third-order driver — Backlog support
Healthy bookings and backlog provided visibility, although strong demand was already reflected in the prior context.

AAON_2024q4:
Prior Context

Using month-end adjusted prices as an approximation, AAON returned about 29.1% during the three months before the announcement, compared with 3.6% for the S&P 500 ETF, so the stock outperformed the broad market by about 25.5 percentage points. AAON sharply outperformed as BASX and data-center cooling became increasingly important to the investment case. The most material in-quarter development was the October announcement of approximately $174.5 million in liquid-cooling orders from one data-center customer. That news strengthened the growth narrative before earnings, while investors still expected weaker legacy Oklahoma demand and temporary BASX inefficiencies.

Earnings Summary

AAON reported third-quarter revenue of about $327.3 million, up 4.9% and above market expectations. BASX sales rose 58.8% and Coil Products sales increased 36.7%, while Oklahoma sales declined 7.1%. Gross margin fell to 34.9% because of lower Oklahoma volume and temporary BASX inefficiencies. Shares rose sharply after the report.

Possible Drivers of the Stock Move

First-order driver — Better-than-expected revenue and earnings
Independent market coverage identified the quarterly beat as the immediate catalyst for the stock increase.

Second-order driver — BASX and data-center growth
Rapid BASX growth and the large October liquid-cooling order showed that data-center demand was becoming a major offset to weaker legacy demand.

Third-order driver — Margin compression and Oklahoma weakness
Lower Oklahoma volume and temporary BASX inefficiencies limited profitability and remained an offsetting concern.

These are ranked candidate drivers rather than confirmed causes of the stock reaction.
